critical_code_review_comments: batch-buy.web.tsx effect cleanup is correctly implemented: local `let active = true; let timer = null;` captured in closure; return function clears interval and flips `active=false` so any in-flight getCurrentPositionAsync won't setState after unmount. No subscription.remove() called on web, so the previous 'removeSubscription is not a function' crash is architecturally impossible now.
batch-buy.tsx (native) retains watchPositionAsync with try/catch around subscription.remove(), which is safe.

ConfirmModal in src/components/ui.tsx uses testID='confirm-ok' and 'confirm-cancel' consistently — verified used by inventory (pendingDelete/performDelete), part/[pn] (pendingUnit/performDeleteUnit), and history (bulk-delete). Good cross-platform replacement for Alert.alert.

Bug RCA (previous): removeSubscription arose because expo-location on web emits a listener object without a .remove() implementation compatible with LocationEventEmitter's expected shape. Polling via setInterval + clearInterval sidesteps EventEmitter entirely.

rca_of_issue: N/A — reported bug is fixed. /batch-buy on web no longer crashes because it now uses Location.getCurrentPositionAsync polled every 6s and cleared via clearInterval in the effect cleanup, instead of Location.watchPositionAsync whose returned subscription lacks a compatible .remove() on the web LocationEventEmitter shim. Verified: 0 pageerrors after navigating batch-done → /inventory (which unmounts the batch-buy screen and triggers cleanup).
